subject: general
question: The _________ considers a marriage as complete and binding at the completion of the Saptapadi ritual.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 7 in The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 says:-**

 
• A** Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies **of either party.
 
• **Rites and ceremonies include the saptapadi.**
 
• It is a ritual of **taking seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire**.
 
• The **marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Saptapadi ceremony:**

 
 
• **Establishes the commitment the couple** makes to each other during the Hindu wedding ceremony.
 
• Saptapadi quite literally** translates from Sanskrit to ‘seven steps’.**
 
• The **couple takes seven full circles,** walking clockwise around the ceremonial fire.
 
• **Circles represent the seven principles and promises they make to each other.​**
 
 
 
• **​**Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
 
 
• India is mainly a Hindu-dominated country.
 
• Therefore, Hindu marriages are mainly governed by “The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.”
 
• ​The Act came into force on May 18, 1955
 
• It is applicable to the whole of India except the state of Jammu & Kashmir.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​​Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1862:**

 
 
• Act consolidates the law related to the **solemnizing of Indian Christian Marriage.**
 
• **Enacted on 18th July 1872.**
 
• Applicable to the** whole of India except Cochin, Manipur, and Jammu & Kashmir.**
 
• The **act contains 88 Sections in 8 Parts and 4 Schedules. ​**
 
 
 
• **Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936:**
 
 
• **​Parsis **are governed in the matters of **marriage and divorce by the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936.**
 
• The **Act is divided into six chapters.**
 
• It **deals with marriage between Parsis,** matrimonial courts, matrimonial suits, children of the parties, and miscellaneous provisions.
 
• **Section 2(7) of the Act says a ‘Parsi’ means a Parsi Zoroastrian.**
 
 
 
• **Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937​**
 
 
• ​The **Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act was passed in 1937.**
 
• The** aim was to formulate an Islamic law code for Indian Muslims.**
 
• For the Muslims on the other hand, the writings in the Quran would be of foremost importance.
 
• **Shariat Application Act, 1937 mandates aspects of Muslim social life such as marriage, divorce,** **inheritance, and family relations.**
 
• The Act lays out that in matters of a personal dispute the State shall not interfere.
